content:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT ALERT - GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION detected in us-west-2 (sev: high). Autoscaler failing with repeated ScaleLimitExceeded. Affected: hosted inference (text-gen), queue growth observed. Paging on-call: @Alice M :rotating_light:

Alice M: on it. seeing the page, pulling up dashboards now. main question: is this only dedicated pools or shared hosted?

Ben I: both. metrics: GPU utilization at 99.9%, queue length for text-gen route up x25 over baseline, 95p latency > 8s. autoscaler logs show repeated errors: 
```
ERROR 2026-03-14T02:07:12Z autoscaler: failed to provision: ScaleLimitExceeded: cannot allocate more gpus for pool: us-west-2-primary
```

Carol S: autoscaler hit configured cluster limit (hard cap) + cloud quota. Also seeing failed spillover attempts in routing logs: requests rejected with 429 because fallback disabled for this route.

Dave P: hmm, routing policy for this customer cohort is "regional_preference" with no cross-region fallback. should have kicked over to eu-west-1. checking routing config now.

Ben I: grabbing the routing logs: 
```
ROUTE_MATCH user:priority=high region=us-west-2 -> pool=us-west-2-primary
QUEUE push -> pool_full -> reject (fallback_allowed=false)
```

Frank N: cloud account limits preventing quick scale. We can spin up a couple emergency spot nodes in us-west-2 but that will take ~6-8m to be ready. eu-west-1 has free capacity but requests are sticky to origin region.

Alice M: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable cross-region spillover policy for text-gen routes to allow eu-west-1 fallback 2) throttle low-priority customers and background batch jobs 3) attempt manual emergency provisioning in us-west-2 4) communicate impact to CS. who can change routing config?

Dave P: I can push routing change. command ready: 
```
# enable soft spillover to eu-west-1 (gradual ramp, preserve locality)
redwoodctl routes update --route text-gen --policy spillover --regions us-west-2,eu-west-1 --spillover-mode soft --max-ramp 20%
```

DeployBot: deploy started for routes/text-gen: spillover config -> soft mode. canary to 5% traffic.

Carol S: also recommend enabling fallback model variant (quantized smaller model) for spillover to reduce GPU footprint. example config: 
```
fallback_model: gpt-small-quant-v1
max_tokens_override: 512
```

Ben I: applying throttle for non-critical customers now: 
```
# lower rate limit for free-tier routes
redwoodctl rates update --selector tier=free --rate 5rps
```

Eve C: drafting customer impact note. earliest ETA for partial mitigation?

Alice M: soft spillover started canary @5% now, watch for errors. manual provisioning in us-west-2 started (Frank). ETA 7m. throttles in place. impact: some users in region will see ~2-4s extra tail latency or fallback to smaller model; heavy requests may be queued/rejected until capacity up.

Ben I: monitoring: within 2m of canary, spillover traffic to eu-west-1 accepted. error rate on spillover path ~1.2% (timeouts), likely cold caches. overall 95p latency across the fleet dropped from 8s -> 3.5s. queue length decreasing.

Frank N: manual nodes active in us-west-2 now, adding to primary pool. provisioning logs: 
```
INFO 2026-03-14T02:15:52Z cloud: launched 4 x a10g-spot
INFO 2026-03-14T02:18:10Z runtime: nodes registered, ready
```

Carol S: autoscaler still reporting ScaleLimitExceeded earlier but now should have room. I'll re-run a synthetic load to validate.

Dave P: rolling the spillover from 5% -> 50% over 10m as long as errors stay <2%. command: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --route text-gen --spillover-ramp 50%
```

Ben I: ramping. metrics: queue length continues to fall, 95p latency trending toward baseline.

Eve C: customer note v1: 
"We experienced degraded performance for text generation in us-west-2 starting 02:06 UTC. Root cause: accelerated demand exhausted GPU capacity and autoscaling hit a quota limit. We have enabled cross-region spillover to eu-west-1, provisioned emergency capacity, and throttled background jobs. Most customers are back to normal, some may still see higher latency or fallback to smaller models. We'll follow up with a detailed post-incident report"

Alice M: good. postmortem owners: Ben + Carol. Eve to coordinate customer communications. Dave to follow up with routing policy changes to avoid sticky regional-only rules. Frank to request quota raises from cloud ops.

DeployBot: route update completed: spillover at 50%.

Carol S: running regression suite, small error spike on eu-west-1 due to KV cache miss but acceptable. watching for model quality drift on fallback model.

Ben I: couple of follow-ups captured: 1) autoscaler needs to account for sudden demand spikes by pre-warming 2) routing default should allow cross-region soft-fallback for critical routes 3) implement circuit-breaker to avoid rejecting when fallback_allowed=false

Alice M: handing off to next on-call (Ben I) in 30m. current status: capacity restored in us-west-2, spillover active at 50%, queue lengths normalizing, most customers recovered. tail-latency still slightly elevated for high-priority large requests.

Ben I: acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor until fully normalized and start the postmortem doc.

Eve C: posting interim update to customers now.

Alice M: incident moved to monitoring state. will close once 24h of stable metrics. great work team :thumbsup:

DeployBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - status: monitoring. incident_ts_end=1769004800

Alice M: final note for handoff: root cause = concurrent demand spike + autoscaler hit hard quota limit + routing config prevented automatic cross-region fallback. mitigation = enabled soft spillover, manual provisioning, throttling, fallback model. action items assigned in postmortem.
